42886294.label: Objective
42886294.text: To develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance.

42886294.label: Materials and methods
42886294.text: The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort. The diagnostic performance of the two scoring models was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). In addition, 352 adnexal lesions from cohorts B and C were included to further evaluate the diagnostic ability of the modified scoring system.

42886294.label: Results
42886294.text: In cohort A, the papillary projections exhibiting the sea anemone sign were highly indicative of borderline lesions (p = 0.001). Diffusion restriction in solid components significantly distinguished benign from malignant masses (p = 0.001). The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) value of cystic components yielded a cutoff of 1.74 (p < 0.05). The DeLong test revealed no statistically significant difference in AUCs between the two systems in cohort A (p > 0.05). The NRI and IDI for the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system were -4.13% and -0.04, respectively (all p > 0.05). In cohorts B and C, the AUCs were 0.933 and 0.910.

42886294.label: Conclusion
42886294.text: The diagnostic efficacy of the modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was comparable to that of the standard O-RADS MRI risk stratification system, facilitating the distinction between benign and malignant adnexal neoplasms.

42886294.label: Key points
42886294.text: Question How can a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system be developed, and can this scoring system accurately classify adnexal masses? Findings The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI system demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance and reliable risk stratification of adnexal masses by evaluating key imaging features. Critical relevance statement The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system contributes to the risk stratification of adnexal masses, particularly for patients who cannot undergo contrast agent administration. This system provides a reliable tool to optimize treatment strategies and improve patient outcomes.

42911394.label: Purpose
42911394.text: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived normalized iodine concentration and extracellular volume fraction for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in patients with Fontan-associated liver disease.

42911394.label: Methods
42911394.text: This single-center exploratory retrospective study included 23 patients with Fontan-associated liver disease who underwent both liver biopsy and delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT between January 2021 and December 2023. Normalized iodine concentration was calculated as hepatic iodine concentration divided by aortic iodine concentration. Hematocrit-adjusted extracellular volume fraction (ECV) was calculated from delayed-phase iodine-density maps. Histologic fibrosis stage based on the METAVIR system was used as the reference standard. Associations between CT biomarkers and fibrosis stage were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test, and Spearman correlation. Diagnostic performance for advanced fibrosis (≥ F3) and cirrhosis (F4) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

42911394.label: Results
42911394.text: Histologic fibrosis stages were F1 in 4 patients, F2 in 2, F3 in 9, and F4 in 8. ECV was higher in advanced fibrosis stages, with median values of 39.21% in F1, 37.15% in F2, 42.72% in F3, and 46.78% in F4. ECV differed significantly among fibrosis stages (p = 0.014), showed a significant ordered trend (p < 0.001), and correlated positively with histologic stage (ρ = 0.666, p < 0.001). IC-normalized showed a weak positive correlation with fibrosis stage, but the ordered trend did not reach statistical significance. For advanced fibrosis, ECV showed promising preliminary discrimination, with an AUC of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.766-1.000). For cirrhosis, ECV showed an AUC of 0.833 (95% CI, 0.655-1.000), with sensitivity of 87.5%, specificity of 80.0%, and negative predictive value of 92.3% at a cutoff of 43.45%.

42911394.label: Conclusion
42911394.text: In this single-center exploratory study, delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived ECV showed a significant association with histologic fibrosis severity and promising preliminary discrimination for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in Fontan-associated liver disease. External validation in larger, independent Fontan cohorts is required before clinical application.

42975644.label: Objective
42975644.text: To investigate the feasibility of automatic training data generation using virtual non-contrast (VNC) images of dual-energy CT and to evaluate the performance of medical segmentation models trained on auto-generated data.

42975644.label: Methods
42975644.text: Training images were generated from contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) scans using VNC algorithm. Corresponding training labels were generated from iodine-density images via intensity thresholding. The paired VNC images and labels constituted the dataset (791 cases in total) for training non-enhanced CT (NECT) segmentation models. We attempted to train segmentation models with VNC images alone, as well as the combination of VNC and real NECT images.

42975644.label: Results
42975644.text: Models trained with auto-generated data effectively performed renal vein segmentation on NECT images, achieving Dice score of 69.60%. It identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks and 54.5% (6/11) accessory veins in the test set. The models' performance on artery segmentation was not satisfactory, with Dice score of 44.56%. It only identified 41.4% (29/70) artery main trunks and 4.54% (1/22) accessory arteries. However, the combination of generated data and labeled data greatly improved model's artery Dice to 71.23%. Combined model identified 100% (70/70) vein main trunks, 98.6% (69/70) artery main trunks, 68.2% (15/22) accessory arteries and 63.6% (7/11) accessory veins. Its accessory artery detection is significantly higher than the model trained with labeled data (15/22 vs. 5/22, p < 0.01), closing the gap with human radiologist (15/22 vs. 18/22, p = 0.250).

42975644.label: Conclusion
42975644.text: VNC and Iodine-density images can be utilized to automatically generate training data for segmentation models. This pipeline shows promise for training segmentation models on NECT images.

42986194.text: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. Results A total of 5110 baseline LDCT examinations were analyzed, including 2343 from NLST and 2767 from P-IELCAP, with 65 lung cancers diagnosed within 1 year. Mean age, mean pack-years, and percentage of female participants were 61.6 years ± 5.1 (SD), 57.3 pack-years ± 24.8, and 39.4% (923 of 2343), respectively, in NLST and 56.0 years ± 9.5, 34.4 pack-years ± 21.5, and 28.6% (791 of 2767), respectively, in P-IELCAP. Lung cancer incidence (per 1000 person-years) was higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (17.7 vs 8.7; P = .006). Mean Sybil 1-year lung cancer probabilities (scaled by 1000 for presentation) were also higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (16.4 vs 9.9; P < .01). Sybil achieved an AUC of 0.93 in both cohorts, whereas the MONAI-based model achieved AUCs of 0.90 in NLST and 0.79 in P-IELCAP. The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity.

43002594.text: 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT is widely used for selecting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) for 177Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy. We present a striking case in which multiple skeletal metastases demonstrated intense, reproducible ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 uptake on post-therapy scintigraphy across all three treatment cycles, yet remained occult or only minimally avid on serial ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT. SPECT/CT confirmed anatomic lesion localization, excluding artifact. This case of "reverse theranostic discordance" challenges the assumption that diagnostic PSMA PET faithfully represents the full target landscape for radioligand therapy. Systematic SPECT/CT review after treatment cycles may reveal therapeutically relevant disease invisible to pretherapy PET.

43008994.label: Objective
43008994.text: To evaluate racial and ethnic differences in longitudinal, age-appropriate breast imaging surveillance among carriers of BRCA1/2 variants.

43008994.label: Materials and methods
43008994.text: This retrospective cohort study included females with pathogenic or likely pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants in the All of Us Research Program. Surveillance was evaluated at semiannual timepoints from 2016-2024 using rolling 12-month windows. Guideline-concordant surveillance was defined as breast MRI at ages 25-29 years and MRI and screening mammography at age 30 years or older. Generalized estimating equation models evaluated racial and ethnic associations in surveillance, adjusting for age, body mass index, Area Deprivation Index, calendar time, and electronic health record (EHR) activity.

43008994.label: Results
43008994.text: Among 6,125 participants, 3,221 (52.6%) were Hispanic, 2,321 (37.9%) non-Hispanic White, 300 (4.9%) non-Hispanic Black, and 283 (4.6%) Other/Multiracial. Compared with non-Hispanic White participants, Hispanic (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.14; 95% CI: 0.08-0.28) and Other/Multiracial participants (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15-0.95) had lower odds of guideline-concordant surveillance. Hispanic participants had lower odds of MRI (aOR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.13-0.37) and mammography (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI: 0.56-0.79); non-Hispanic Black participants had lower odds of mammography (aOR, 0.57; 95% CI: 0.36-0.91). Over time, the difference in the odds of screening mammography between Hispanic and non-Hispanic White participants widened (OR per year, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99).

43008994.label: Conclusion
43008994.text: Racial and ethnic differences in guideline-concordant breast imaging surveillance were observed among BRCA1/2 variant carriers, particularly among Hispanic participants, indicating persistent disparities in recommended surveillance within this high-risk population.

43064644.label: Background
43064644.text: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.

43064644.label: Methods
43064644.text: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.

43064644.label: Results
43064644.text: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.

43064644.label: Conclusion
43064644.text: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

43071594.label: Background
43071594.text: This study aimed to perform a preliminary, intraindividual comparison of [68Ga]Ga-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-46 and [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-(Tyr³)-octreotate (DOTATATE) PET/CT for meningioma imaging. While [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET, targeting somatostatin receptor 2, is established in meningioma evaluation, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI PET, targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP) in the tumor microenvironment, offers a novel diagnostic approach.

43071594.label: Patients and methods
43071594.text: Five female patients with meningiomas underwent both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT scans. A comprehensive comparison was conducted at both patient and lesion levels. Quantitative parameters, including maximum and mean standardized uptake values (SUVmax, SUVmean), metabolic tumor volumes [FAP expression tumor volume, somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-expressing tumor volume], and total lesion expression (total lesion FAP expression, total lesion SSTR expression), were analyzed.

43071594.label: Results
43071594.text: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET demonstrated superior lesion detection, identifying 21 lesions compared with 19 detected by [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET. At both patient and lesion levels, [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE showed significantly higher tracer uptake and total lesion expression. The patient-level median SUVmax was 27.3 for [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE versus 6.93 for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 (P = 0.04). At the lesion level, the median SUVmax was 10.63 for [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE versus 2.52 for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 (P = 0.0001). Despite these differences, significant positive correlations were observed between the quantitative parameters of both tracers at the lesion level (eg, SUVmax R = 0.69, P = 0.001; total lesion FAP expression/total lesion SSTR expression R = 0.84, P = 0.0001). In addition, both FAP-expressing tumor volume and SSTR-expressing tumor volume strongly correlated with MRI tumor size.

43071594.label: Conclusions
43071594.text: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET demonstrated superior lesion detection and significantly higher uptake intensity in meningiomas compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET, reinforcing DOTATATE PET's established role as a highly effective imaging modality. The lower yet present FAPI uptake and the strong positive correlation between the two tracers suggest a potential complementary role for FAPI imaging, possibly reflecting an interplay between tumor cells and their microenvironment. These preliminary findings warrant further investigation in larger prospective studies.

43078994.label: Purpose
43078994.text: Detecting residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) by MRI is challenging due to post-surgical or post-radiotherapy tissue remodeling. While [11C]Methionine ([11C]MET) PET demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for RPA, its use is limited to centers with an on-site cyclotron. [18F]Fluorocholine ([18F]FCH) PET, which has shown incidental uptake in pituitary adenomas, may offer a viable alternative. This study compared dual-phase [18F]FCH with [11C]MET PET imaging for localizing suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) and characterizing uptake differences between suspected RPA and pituitary gland remnant (PGR) after surgery.

43078994.label: Methods
43078994.text: This retrospective study included 23 patients addressed during the follow-up of an ablated pituitary adenoma (n = 23). The presence of suspected RPA was determined by multidisciplinary consensus integrating postoperative metabolic imaging, serial MRI follow-up, and biochemical data. Two patients underwent reoperation, in whom histopathological confirmation was available. All patients underwent a standard [11C]MET PET/MRI acquisition (mean activity = 397 ± 51 MBq) and subsequently a 20-min dynamic [18F]FCH PET/MRI acquisition, followed by an additional late static [18F]FCH PET/CT acquisition performed at 40-55 min post-FCH injection (mean activity = 334 ± 77 MBq). RPA and PGR uptake were compared visually and quantitatively using maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) for both tracers.

43078994.label: Results
43078994.text: All lesions suspected of representing RPA were visually detected on both early and late [18F]FCH images. In suspected RPA, [18F]FCH uptake was comparable to [11C]MET uptake, with mean SUVmax values of 6.2 ± 2.3 for early (3-20 min post-injection) [18F]FCH PET, 5.1 ± 2.3 for late [18F]FCH PET, and 5.5 ± 1.9 for [11C]MET (p = 0.11 and 0.51, respectively). Both suspected RPA and PGR showed decreasing [18F]FCH uptake over time, with a significantly greater decline in PGR (early PET SUVmax: 5.7 ± 1.5; late PET SUVmax: 3.7 ± 1.1; time-by-region interaction, p < 0.0001). Accordingly, the RPA/PGR SUVmax ratio was significantly lower on early [18F]FCH images than on late [18F]FCH images (p = 0.0014) and [11C]MET images (p < 0.001), whereas it did not differ significantly between late [18F]FCH and [11C]MET images (p > 0.5).

43078994.label: Conclusion
43078994.text: [18F]FCH PET/MRI demonstrated uptake in lesions suspected of representing RPA, with uptake levels comparable to those observed with [11C]MET PET/MRI. The greater decline in PGR uptake on delayed imaging improved the quantitative RPA/PGR contrast, supporting dual-time-point [18F]FCH PET/MRI as a promising approach for postoperative tissue discrimination. These exploratory findings require prospective validation using an independent reference standard.
